item.title: Senate GOP group pours millions into defending Kansas seat
item.description: The race for control of the Senate is changing in the final weeks before the midterms, with the GOP defending several traditionally red-leaning states.

item.title: FlyDubai pilot tells his survival story in emotional call with Indian leader
item.description: The FlyDubai captain attacked by his co-pilot tells his harrowing survival story to India's leader in an emotional video call from his hospital bed.

item.title: Details emerge in case of former Cornell student alleging rape by frat members
item.description: A woman, identified only as Jane Doe, alleges she was gang-raped by seven fraternity members in 2024 and accuses Cornell University of failing to protect her.

item.title: A valet became a key source of support for cancer patients at a N.Y. care center
item.description: Jon Avery, who parks cars at the Roswell Cancer Center in Buffalo, New York, says his goal when interacting with patients is to "have a meaningful encounter that's not hollow."

item.title: Professor to present findings questioning whether Epstein killed himself
item.description: Michael Freeman plans to publish his research and the New York City Medical Examiner's Epstein autopsy files.

item.title: FlyDubai co-pilot had previously been fired from Oman Air for "extremist views," sources said
item.description: The FlyDubai co-pilot who allegedly tried to crash an Israel-bound flight this week was fired from Oman Air for "extremist views," sources say. CBS News' Imtiaz Tyab reports.

item.title: Vance says Senate candidate Angie Nixon doesn't belong in America
item.description: Vice President JD Vance on Thursday said U.S. Senate candidate Angie Nixon doesn't belong in America because she's a democratic socialist. Politco's Riley Rogerson and Semafor's Nicholas Wu joins "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: Breast cancer survivor attributes recovery to kindness of hospital valet
item.description: Jon Avery, who parks cars at the Roswell Cancer Center in Buffalo, New York, is being credited with helping patients fight their battles with the disease. Steve Hartman goes on the road.

item.title: Texas Tech megadonor voices support for NIL legislation, talks collective bargaining
item.description: Cody Campbell, the chair of the Texas Tech Board of Regents and a major donor for the school, joins "The Takeout" to discuss his support for the Protect College Sports Act.

item.title: Students lead violent protests in France over underfunding, overcrowding in schools
item.description: Students in France are leading violent protests over poor conditions in the country's educational institutions. Holly Williams has the story.

item.title: What AI could mean for the next generation of workers
item.description: AI is changing many of the tasks traditionally handled by entry-level workers. Tech executive Clara Shih discusses what that could mean for the next generation of employees Sunday on 60 Minutes.

item.title: Trump continues midterms push in Alabama as his approval rating nears record low over economy
item.description: President Trump continued his extended midterm campaign in support of fellow Republicans on Friday with a stop in deep-red Mobile, Alabama. Weijia Jiang has the details.

item.title: FlyDubai captain stabbed mid-flight by "radicalized" co-pilot speaks out
item.description: Captain Smit Machchhar, who was stabbed while flying an Israel-bound plane, shared new details about the incident from his hospital bed. Imtiaz Tyab reports.

item.title: CBS News poll finds voters split on state v. national focus in Maine Senate race
item.description: Troy Jackson is boosted by those looking for change, while Collins peels off some Trump disapprovers.

item.title: Susan Collins tied with Troy Jackson in Maine Senate race, new CBS News poll shows
item.description: Democrat Troy Jackson has pulled into a tie with Republican Sen. Susan Collins in Maine's battle for U.S. Senate. Zachary Donnini, head of data science at VoteHub, joins "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: Jane Doe's attorney speaks to CBS News about Cornell rape investigation
item.description: Thomas Giuffra, the attorney who filed Jane Doe's civil lawsuit in the Cornell rape investigation, shared new details with CBS News about his client's allegations. Lilia Luciano reports.

item.title: U.S. job growth cools, unemployment ticks up in last jobs report before midterms
item.description: The last jobs report before the 2026 midterms was underwhelming, with some unhappy revisions to previous upbeat reports. CBS News' Kelly O'Grady reports.

item.title: How Trump's foreign policy is impacting the midterms as third aircraft carrier moves to Middle East
item.description: A third U.S. aircraft carrier is heading to the Middle East along with thousands of troops. CBS News chief foreign affairs correspondent Margaret Brennan reports and Matt Kroenig, nonresident senior fellow at the Atlantic Council, joins to discuss the war.

item.title: FlyDubai co-pilot was fired from Oman Air job for "extremist views," sources say
item.description: The co-pilot who earlier this week allegedly made a violent attempt to crash a passenger aircraft was previously fired from a position with Oman Air for holding "extremist views," multiple sources told CBS News.

item.title: Judge says federal law banning noncitizen voting is unconstitutional
item.description: In a possible blow to the Trump administration's efforts to charge noncitizens with voting, a judge has dismissed a case against a Jamaican national accused of illegally voting, finding the law she was charged under is unconstitutional.

item.title: Newly released footage shows Luigi Mangione's arrest in Pennsylvania
item.description: Body camera video shows Altoona police arresting Luigi Mangione, questioning him about a fake ID and recovering evidence later linked to the fatal shooting of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson.

item.title: Major Garrett on Trump's announcements of several investment projects
item.description: This week brought a flurry of announcements from the Trump White House desperate to alter savagely sour assessment of the economy and the president's performance. Major Garrett breaks it all down.

item.title: Jane Doe's attorney says "she was incapable of consent," alleges cover-up
item.description: Jane Doe's attorney, Thomas Giuffra, tells CBS News the investigation into her alleged rape at a Cornell fraternity was a failure and university police "were in over their heads."

item.title: Jane Doe's lawyer accuses Cornell of a "cover-up"
item.description: Jane Doe's lawyer Thomas Giuffra is accusing the university of a "cover-up," claiming school officials were more focused on protecting Cornell's reputation than seeking accountability.

item.title: Jane Doe's lawyer says "she was incapable of consent" on night of alleged rape at Cornell frat house
item.description: Thomas Giuffra, the lawyer for Jane Doe, says she was "incapable of consent" because she was "completely, grossly intoxicated" the night she was allegedly raped at a Cornell fraternity house in October 2024.

item.title: Feds charge shop clerk, son with selling illegal kratom after 2 Ole Miss deaths
item.description: Federal authorities investigating the deaths of two University of Mississippi students have charged a store clerk and his son with selling an illegal kratom product.

item.title: In Cornell investigation, Gov. Hochul says AG James will find out "how was this woman denied justice"
item.description: Gov. Kathy Hochul has tapped New York Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor in the Cornell University alleged rape case.

item.title: David Rivera sentenced to 10 years in Venezuela lobbying case
item.description: Former U.S. Rep. David Rivera was convicted on federal charges stemming from a secret lobbying campaign tied to the Venezuelan government.

item.title: Christa Pike critically ill, intubated after botched execution, attorneys say
item.description: Christa Pike "remains critically ill" and is receiving medical care after a botched execution attempt in Tennessee, her attorneys said.

item.title: American Airlines will let travelers mix cash and miles to pay for flights
item.description: As holiday airfares spike, American Airlines plans to let travelers pay for flights with a mix of cash and loyalty points.
